findings.evidence: Fig. 3.4 caption text in body text: "i.e. ~12 GB vs ~0.6 GB for the 9.2K input. The gap is the shape, not the routing: a dense model with the challenger's shape holds the same ~0.6 GB" followed by the run-off fragment "holds h 6 GB"
findings.issue: Textual well-formedness defect: a duplicated/garbled clause "holds h 6 GB" appears immediately after a complete sentence stating the same fact — a truncation artifact where "holds the same ~0.6 GB" was partially re-emitted. This is exactly the sort of duplicated-clause defect the previous round missed.
findings.fix_instruction: Delete the stray fragment "holds h 6 GB" and ensure the sentence ends with "holds the same ~0.6 GB".

findings.evidence: Ch. 3 §3.1.1 and Fig. 3.2 caption: "Full-canvas masked sampler: accept selected IDs ... Full bidirectional forwards: fixed IDs can still acquire new K/V." Fig. 3.2 caption: "in the full-canvas masked panel, accepted IDs become fixed resolved positions out of order and do not form a contiguous prefix until finalization."
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption consistency defect: the figure's own lane label says a full-canvas masked sampler with 'fixed prompt' and 'repeat evaluations' produces 'A ? C ?' — i.e. accepted IDs out of order with the prompt held fixed — while the caption states accepted IDs 'become fixed resolved positions'. The in-panel note 'Here, accepted IDs stay fixed; prompt-state reuse is not assumed' plus the 'Full bidirectional forwards: fixed IDs can still acquire new K/V' note means accepted IDs are not truly 'fixed' in the memory sense, yet the caption calls them 'fixed resolved positions'. The caption's 'Solid brackets identify finalized prefix state' then has no bracket in the full-canvas panel, which is not stated.
findings.fix_instruction: In Fig. 3.2's caption, replace 'fixed resolved positions' with 'resolved (accepted) positions whose K/V may still be recomputed' and add 'the full-canvas panel has no finalized prefix bracket, because no contiguous prefix exists until finalization.'

findings.evidence: Fig 3.4 caption ends: "The gap is the shape, not the routing: a dense model with the challenger's shape holds h 6 GB" (PDF p.100 / book p.76).
findings.issue: Caption text is corrupted: 'holds h 6 GB' should read 'holds ~0.6 GB' (the 8-bit challenger KV figure established in §3.3.3 and Table 3-3: 9,200 × 0.0655 MB ≈ 0.60 GB). As printed it reads as '6 GB' — a 10× misread of the very number the caption is arguing ('~12 GB vs ~0.6 GB').
findings.fix_instruction: Restore the mangled '~0.6 GB' (or '≈0.60 GB') in the caption's final sentence.

Figure text: "Accepted IDs extend the prefix; K/V are cached when processed." Caption: "In the autoregressive and valid block-causal panels, accepted IDs extend the prefix; in the full-canvas masked panel, accepted IDs become fixed resolved positions out of order and do not form a contiguous prefix until finalization."
findings.issue: The in-figure note states a rule without its panel qualifier, even though the caption says the rule does not apply to the full-canvas masked sampler. This can mislead a reader into treating accepted IDs as a reusable contiguous prefix in all samplers.
findings.fix_instruction: Qualify the in-figure sentence, e.g. "In autoregressive and valid block-causal panels, accepted IDs extend the prefix; K/V are cached when processed," and add the full-canvas exception directly in the figure body.
